claims.text: Preheating the build platform to approximately 300°C during SLM of CoCrFeNiMn will reduce thermal gradients.
Reducing thermal gradients through platform preheating will reduce residual stresses.
Platform preheating will improve the dimensional precision of SLM-fabricated CoCrFeNiMn components.
Platform preheating will improve the mechanical integrity of SLM-fabricated CoCrFeNiMn components.
Platform preheating will reduce fabrication-induced defects in SLM-fabricated CoCrFeNiMn components.
Room-temperature-platform SLM of CoCrFeNiMn produces significant thermal gradients.
The thermal gradients in baseline SLM processing lead to residual stresses, warping, and microstructural defects.
High-purity inert gas or vacuum conditions prevent oxidation during the proposed SLM process.
Reduced residual stress enables a more uniform microstructure.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stress produce fewer pores and other defects.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stress reduce warping of finished parts.
Elevating substrate temperature decreases the temperature differential between the molten material and the build platform.
A smaller melt-to-platform temperature differential reduces thermal shock.
Preheating the substrate produces a slower cooling rate.
The slower cooling rate decreases residual stress.
The slower cooling rate produces a refined grain structure.
The proposed microstructural changes enhance interlayer bonding.
Components built on the preheated platform will exhibit approximately 15% or greater reduction in warping or distortion relative to the room-temperature-platform baseline.
Components built on the preheated platform will have improved tensile and fatigue strength relative to the baseline.
The benefits of platform preheating depend on effective oxidation prevention, and excessive substrate temperature or inadequate atmospheric control may negate them.
